newsitem.title: DENMARK: Bill would hit Tele Danmark profit - union.
newsitem.headline: Bill would hit Tele Danmark profit - union.

text.p: Denmark's telecommunication union said on Wednesday draft telecoms legislation on interconnection deals under deregulation could cut profits by about one billion crowns and lead to more job losses for telecoms group Tele Danmark.
"Company calculations show that the impact on an annual basis would be 1.2 billion crowns, corresponding to just below one billion crowns after tax," union chairman Bo Stenoer Larsen told Reuters.
He said that he feared this would mean a direct fall in Tele Danmark's profit.

"The draft legislation will put Tele Danmark under such pressure that it will be forced to make further cuts in staff beyond those already announced," the union said in a separate statement issued earlier on Wednesday.
"The prices for competitors' access to Tele Danmark's network are far too low," it said.
Tele Danmark unveiled in late January plans to make net cuts of 2,000 of its present 16,500 staff as part of a streamlining programme.
On February 20 Tele Danmark's board chairman wrote to Danish research minister Jytte Hilden in protest against the government's proposed telecommunications legislation.
"In its draft the government is proposing competitors' access fees to Tele Danmark's network below bottom level long-run incremental costs," a Tele Danmark spokesman told Reuters on Monday.

"This is much lower than European Union fee stipulations and would hit Tele Danmark hard, causing us major losses. It could have the most serious economic consequences for Tele Danmark of all the liberalisation measures so far," the spokesman said.
The Danish telecommunications sector was deregulated on July 1, 1996 and the second phase enabling legislation is due to go through parliament next month.
Tele Danmark reported a 1995 net profit of 3.49 billion crowns.
